_note: How the animals are rendered (scene.py, cartoon.py, sprites.py). view_transform and view_look: Blender's color management (Standard keeps cartoon colors as painted; the look adds contrast). lights: sun strengths and colors (key from the front-top, a soft warm fill so shadows aren't gray, a gentle rim). skin: the cartoon skin's material (low sheen and subsurface so colors stay solid, not hazy). color_smoothing: rounds of evening out the painted vertex colors so color borders (a fox's bib, ear tips) come out as clean, even edges instead of streaks along the mesh's triangles (color_smoothing_strength: how much each round moves toward the neighbors). outline: the dark cartoon line (pixels at sprite_pixels_per_tile; scaled with the resolution) and its color. sprite_pixels_per_tile: render resolution of the battle sprites (pixels per field tile); sprite_samples / portrait_samples: Cycles samples per pixel (with denoising). portrait_size: the card picture's size in pixels. max_sheet: the largest sprite-sheet page (pixels on a side); a bigger sheet is split into pages. padding: transparent pixels round every frame (so smooth filtering and smaller mip levels don't bleed into a neighbor). import: how Godot stores the art (set_import.py): "lossless" (exactly as rendered), "lossy" (one WebP pass) or "basis" (GPU-compressed Basis Universal UASTC). Sprite sheets are lossless: Basis was tried (a quarter of the memory at twice the resolution) but left faint 4x4 block ghosts in the soft shadows and edges, and about twice the download; lossy WebP blurs colors at the dark outline. Sheets have no mipmaps (they are drawn near their real size; mipmaps would add a third more memory). Portraits and arenas keep mipmaps (they are shown much smaller than they are). uastc_level and rdo_quality_loss: Basis settings, if used.

outline._note: sprite_pixels is at 56 pixels a tile (scaled with sprite_pixels_per_tile); portrait_pixels at a 512-pixel portrait.

import._models_note: The 3D viewer's models (art/models/*.glb): no tangents (no normal maps), no LODs or shadow meshes (one animal, close up, no real lights), no light baking. Less to download and to keep in memory.
import._arenas_note: Arena pictures are rendered lossless and compressed once here (lossy WebP). An older picture saved lossy is kept lossless instead, so it isn't compressed twice (set_import.py checks).

model._note: The real-3D models for the animal viewer (export_gltf.py): about `triangles` triangles for the body, animations sampled at keys_per_second, and which animations (the viewer idles and plays the others when tapped). battle: the fights' lighter models (game/art/models/battle/): about `triangles` for the body, each eye, ear or claw cut to piece_triangles, every animation a fight plays, and models.json with each one's size in field tiles.
